regime: Post-Fed relief inside a still-restrictive capital regime; oil scarcity premium easing as logistics adapt, while refined-product tightness remains important
whatIsNewNow: Post-Fed market transmission improved: S&P 500 +1.1%, Nasdaq +1.7%, US 10Y retreated to about 4.93% after briefly clearing 5% on the decision day. This weakens the '5% and rising' impulse without ending capital scarcity.

Energy scarcity is becoming less one-way: Brent fell toward ~$103 as Saudi crude rerouting through Oman increased, but diesel/refined-product supply remains tight enough to keep products above crude in the hierarchy.

YTLPOWR rebounded to RM5.66 after reserving four additional Siemens Energy gas turbines; seven reserved turbines now represent about 5.25GW. This is company-specific confirmation of Malaysia power/data-centre optionality, but capex/funding/energisation remain the proof gates.
XOM fell to $163.27 as the geopolitical crude premium eased; the prior $164-166 reclaim failed and becomes resistance/reclaim rather than support.
TTWO closed about $210.77 after trading to $207.77, meaning the ~$210 reassessment line is being tested rather than cleanly holding.
TSLA rebounded to about $367.86 but remains below the $375-383 confirmation band.
LNG/Cheniere closed about $269.83, now at/below the old excellent $270-275 entry area while the structural LNG-rerouting thesis remains intact. This materially improves entry asymmetry.
whatMattersMostNow: Whether the 10Y remains below 5% after the Fed/BOJ sequence; capital scarcity is still the governing portfolio filter.
Refined-product/diesel inventories and cracks versus crude as Saudi/Oman rerouting reduces crude scarcity.
Funded and energised AI/power capacity rather than requested MW; backlog cash conversion is the decisive proof point.
LNG replacement/rerouting demand and Cheniere entry asymmetry near $270.
Whether YTLPOWR's turbine reservations become contracted, funded generation/data-centre cash flow.
Weak-end credit stress, consumer/housing sensitivity and breadth under still-high real/nominal yields.
